catalyst_text: Presented positive Phase 3 subgroup analysis at EHA
detailed_catalyst_text: A post-hoc subgroup analysis from the pivotal Phase 3 EPCORE FL-1 trial in relapsed or refractory follicular lymphoma showed consistent, sustained efficacy for epcoritamab plus rituximab and lenalidomide across multiple risk and fitness subgroups. Results included PFS hazard ratios below 0.3 and higher ORR and CRR versus R2 alone, and were delivered in an oral presentation at EHA 2026. Safety was manageable with no new signals identified, reinforcing the regimen’s clinical benefit.
catalyst_text_evidence: Genmab A/S (NASDAQ:GMAB) today announced new data from a post-hoc subgroup analysis from the pivotal Phase 3 EPCORE® FL-1 trial, evaluating epcoritamab, a subcutaneous T-cell engaging bispecific antibody, in combination with rituximab and lenalidomide (epcoritamab + R2) in adult patients with relapsed or refractory (R/R) follicular lymphoma (FL), which showed that epcoritamab + R2 delivered consistent and sustained efficacy benefits across clinically relevant subgroups, including Follicular Lymphoma International Prognostic Index (FLIPI) score (0–2 vs 3–5), progression of disease less than or equal to two years from the date of initial frontline therapy (POD24) (POD24 vs non-POD24), and patient fitness (non-Hodgkin lymphoma 5 score). These results were presented during an oral presentation (abstract S229) at the European Hematology Association (EHA) 2026 Congress held in Stockholm, Sweden, 2026-06-11 - 2026-06-14. The data demonstrated that progression-free survival (PFS) benefits continued to favor epcoritamab + R2, with hazard ratios (HR) consistently below 0.3 across FLIPI 0–2 (0.18 [0.10–0.33]) and FLIPI 3–5 (0.25 [0.15–0.42]), POD24 (HR 0.22 [95% CI 0.13–0.37]), and non-Hodgkin lymphoma 5 (NHL-5) subgroups (low: HR 0.27 [0.17–0.42]; H+I, high and intermediate: HR 0.14 [0.06–0.29]), indicating a substantially reduced risk of disease progression or death. The safety profile of epcoritamab + R2 was manageable across all patient subgroups and consistent with that observed in the overall trial population, with no new safety signals identified.

catalyst_text: Presented positive first-line DLBCL results at EHA
detailed_catalyst_text: New first-line DLBCL results were reported from a Phase 2 monotherapy trial (EPCORE DLBCL-3; ORR 67%, CR 58%) and from a Phase 1b/2 combination trial with R-mini-CHOP (EPCORE NHL-2; ORR 93%, CR 86%) in elderly or comorbidity-ineligible patients. The data were presented at the EHA 2026 Congress, and the DLBCL-3 results were simultaneously published in The Lancet Haematology. These findings support potential utility in frail, newly diagnosed patients with limited treatment options.
catalyst_text_evidence: "The results from both studies were presented in two poster presentations (abstracts PS2082 and PF1007) at the European Hematology Association (EHA) 2026 Congress held in Stockholm, Sweden, 2026-06-11 to 2026-06-14." "Additionally, the full EPCORE DLBCL-3 results have been simultaneously published in The Lancet Haematology." "Results from the Phase 2 EPCORE® DLBCL-3 study showed an overall response rate (ORR) of 67% and a complete response (CR) rate of 58% with epcoritamab monotherapy in elderly patients with newly diagnosed DLBCL." "In the Phase 1b/2 EPCORE NHL-2 study, epcoritamab plus rituximab plus dose-attenuated cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, and prednisone (R-mini-CHOP) demonstrated an ORR of 93% and a CR rate of 86% in elderly patients with newly diagnosed DLBCL."

drug_indication: Relapsed or Refractory Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma
catalyst_text: Announced positive topline results in relapsed refractory DLBCL
detailed_catalyst_text: Topline data from a randomized Phase 3 trial in adults with relapsed or refractory diffuse large B-cell lymphoma ineligible for transplant showed epcoritamab monotherapy improved progression-free survival and other efficacy measures. Overall survival did not reach statistical significance. These results support the therapy’s potential benefit in this difficult-to-treat population.
catalyst_text_evidence: Genmab A/S (NASDAQ:GMAB) today announced topline results from the Phase 3 EPCORE DLBCL-1 trial evaluating epcoritamab, a T-cell engaging bispecific antibody administered subcutaneously, which demonstrated an improvement in progression-free survival (PFS) (HR: 0.74 [95% CI 0.60 to 0.92])* in patients treated with epcoritamab monotherapy. Additionally, improvements were observed in the complete response rate, duration of response, and time to next treatment among patients treated with epcoritamab monotherapy. The study demonstrated an overall survival (OS) of HR: 0.96 [95% CI 0.77 to 1.20], which did not reach statistical significance. The global study enrolled 483 patients with R/R DLBCL with at least one prior line of therapy (73% had received two or more prior lines) who were ineligible for high-dose chemotherapy and autologous stem cell transplant (HDT-ASCT).

catalyst_text: Presented encouraging Phase 2 Richter transformation results ASH
detailed_catalyst_text: New and updated data from the Phase 2 expansion cohorts of EPCORE CLL-1 in Richter transformation were presented in oral sessions at a major hematology conference. The monotherapy and combination arms showed encouraging response and survival outcomes, and results from the monotherapy arm were simultaneously published in The Lancet Haematology. These findings support the therapeutic potential in patients with this aggressive CLL transformation.
